A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same generative contextual Thompson sampling work. The main text, figures, algorithms, equations, and complete theory and experimental appendices are readable in both versions, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic and MIND-based semisynthetic bandit experiments, including algorithm comparisons in Figure 5 and training-data and policy-class analyses in Figures 7–8.

after.justification: v2 reports original bandit comparisons and supplementary experiments in Figures 6 and 8–12, plus measured computational costs in Appendix B.8.

M1.justification: The central impute–fit–act procedure in Algorithm 1 remains unchanged. v2 introduces context sampling through the learned model instead of a known context distribution, replaces boosted-tree policy fitting with MLP fitting in the semisynthetic implementation, and adds truncated-imputation variants. These modify components of the existing framework.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic logistic bandits and the same MIND-based semisynthetic news-recommendation setting. Added horizon and model-depth experiments vary configurations within this coverage. Nonstationarity, correlated outcomes, and fairness constraints are discussed but are not evaluated as additional task scenarios.

E2.justification: v2 Figure 6 adds fitted-prior TS-Linear and TS-Neural-Linear with both uninformative and fitted priors, substantially expanding controls for representation learning and prior information. Greedy, epsilon-greedy, ordinary TS-Linear, and LinUCB remain. Softmax is retained against TS-Gen in Appendix B.7, Figure 12, rather than removed from the paper.

E3.justification: The semisynthetic policy and regret oracle change from boosted trees to an MLP. v1 Appendix B.3.1 explicitly fixes contexts known before evaluation; v2 describes sampling future contexts using an empirical distribution learned from training contexts. Added protocols include 80/20 splits for prior fitting, imputation horizons of 100–500, and sequence-model depth sweeps. The overall 500-step, ten-action setting remains.

E4.justification: v2 adds imputation-horizon sensitivity experiments in Figure 10, sequence-model depth ablations in Figure 11, and generation-versus-policy-fitting cost measurements in Appendix B.8. The existing loss-versus-regret analysis remains, while the policy-class analysis replaces the tree-based comparison with an MLP comparison. These additions substantially broaden diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: Regret reporting continues to use 500 bandit environments and error bars of plus or minus one standard error. v2 additionally reports timing means and standard deviations, specifying 20 tasks and 10,000 decisions. Its timing prose is inconsistent about task-level versus decision-level aggregation. Neither version establishes repeated training seeds or significance testing.

E6.justification: The main comparison curves are revised and expanded; for example, the synthetic plots reverse the ordering of LinUCB and ordinary TS-Linear. Semisynthetic curves use a changed policy and oracle, so their lower plotted regret is not a directly comparable performance gain. v2 adds horizon/depth results and timing measurements, including 6.4 seconds per decision for MLP-policy TS-Gen versus 1.9 for neural-linear TS.

T1.justification: v2 removes the former global environment assumptions from its regret statements, incorporates contexts into the prediction loss, and changes the entropy term from conditioning on both Z and X1:T to conditioning only on Z. It adds a probability-matching proof, multiclass Natarajan-dimension claims, an information-ratio bound, and linear/logistic comparisons. Appendix A is substantially revised; the complexity proof still uses fixed-context labeling counts despite removing context conditioning.

C1.justification: The central contribution of generative Thompson sampling with loss-dependent regret remains. However, v2 substantially broadens its claimed applicability beyond v1's stationary, independent-action, known-context formulation, explicitly encompassing nonstationary environments and correlated outcomes. It presents the practical implementation as a specialization of this more general framework.

C2.justification: v2 adds explicit limitations concerning proof-of-concept evaluation, incomplete historical datasets, heuristic reconstruction, and computational expense. It expands interpretation of misspecification-loss scaling and explains why specialized linear-bandit bounds can be tighter. The attribution of gains over LinUCB and TS-Linear to pretraining and prior information is qualified as a conjecture, and computational mitigation strategies are discussed.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands reproducibility information: explicit bootstrap pseudocode, empirical context-distribution construction, detailed MLP policy settings, fitted-prior estimation and regularization, CPU memory requirements, training and decision times, and model/data access and license information. The existing sequence architecture is explained more precisely; its new recurrent-network description alone does not establish an architectural replacement.

R1.justification: v2 adds substantive meta-bandit positioning, including comparisons with Basu, Boutilier, Hong, and other approaches. It expands connections to multiclass complexity theory, Bayesian prediction and misspecification, fairness, and efficient inference. Appendix A.6 provides explicit comparisons with existing linear and logistic regret bounds. These changes go beyond switching from numbered to author-year citations.

P1.justification: The narrative is extensively rewritten and reorganized. v1's separated conceptual and imperfect-model regret discussions become a unified general algorithm/theory section followed by practical implementation. Environment assumptions are reframed as implementation approximations, and the appendices gain a more detailed hierarchy. Terminology, explanations, limitations, and author information also change.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a substantially different conference layout, title block, typography, and figure placement, including text wrapped around smaller diagrams. It adds a potential-outcomes diagram and horizon/depth plots, redraws the main comparison with a shared external legend, and presents Softmax separately. Existing diagrams and analyses are also resized and relocated rather than all being newly introduced.

improvement.justification: v2 improves empirical scrutiny through stronger baselines, ablations, timing measurements, and fuller implementation and limitations reporting. However, v1's complexity bound conditions on X1:T, whereas v2 Proposition 2 removes that conditioning while Appendix A.3 still counts labelings of fixed contexts. That argument does not account for entropy contributed by random contexts, leaving a central revised regret-rate claim unsupported as written. These empirical gains and substantive theoretical concerns prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
